Definition: neuter of a presumed derivative of the original form of τλάω (to bear; equivalent to G5342); a balance (as supporting weights), i.e. (by implication) a certain weight (and thence a coin or rather sum of money) or "talent":--talent.
BiblicalUsage: The talent was the largest weight of money, and Jesus builds two parables on it. In Matthew 18 a servant owes ten thousand talents, a debt no man could pay. In Matthew 25 the master gives five talents, two, and one, each according to ability, and asks for an account on his return. The word is a balance first, then a sum, then a trust.
TheologicalSignificance: The parable of the talents, I hold, is about stewardship, not arithmetic. I believe God gives each of us according to our ability, and He will ask what we did with it — and the servant who buried his talent is the warning I take personally. Faithfulness, not size, is what the master praises.
